gap: No result ChatGPT got states that two BLUETTI 350W panels (33 V open-circuit voltage, or Voc, each) wired in series reach 66 V, over the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2's 12–60 V solar input. BLUETTI sells exactly that pair as the $2,148 'Elite 200 V2+2*350W Solar' bundle, so those panels must be wired in parallel. Two BLUETTI 200W (SP200L) panels in series reach 49.2 V, which is within the limit.
standout_why: I compared five pages. EnergySage (cited) only says to 'choose your own panels as long as they fall within the power station's solar input specs', with no figures and no warning about series wiring. OutdoorGearLab (cited) lists adapter-cable traps (Jackery, DJI, Goal Zero) but nothing on panel voltage or series/parallel wiring. BackupPowerHub's home-backup page covers the Elite 200 V2 (120 V only, can't add batteries, 15 ms UPS switchover) and its fridge page covers surge and UPS settings, but neither mentions Voc, series/parallel wiring or the 60 V limit. backup-power.org was not opened. The finding is new and useful. It decides how the bundle is wired more than which products go in it, so it scores 2, not 3.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh, 120 V). It already has a backup page and ready-made solar bundles. Its PV input is 12–60 V / 20 A, 1,000 W max, according to BLUETTI's US page.

Solar panels: 2× BLUETTI 200W (SP200L) for series wiring, because 2 × 24.6 V = 49.2 V Voc, which is under 60 V. If you choose 2× BLUETTI 350W instead, wire them in parallel only, because 2 × 33 V = 66 V Voc in series is over 60 V.
Solar cable: an MC4-to-XT60 cable. BLUETTI's 350W panel ships with a 20 A, 1.5 m one. The Elite 200 V2's own in-box list has no solar cable.

items: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×350W Solar bundle (wire in parallel only) | https://www.bluettipower.com/products/elite-200-v2-2-pv350d | $2,148.00 | 2026-11-10

findings.label: Solar (PV) input limit
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2+2*350W Solar (BLUETTI US store)
findings.note: From the page FAQ: 'PV input: Elite 200 V2: 12V-60V/20A, 1,000W max'. The same line appears on the 2×200W bundle page.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage (Voc)
findings.note: Two in series: 2 × 33 V = 66 V, which is 6 V over the Elite 200 V2's 60 V input ceiling. That is at standard test conditions; Voc rises in cold weather (not quantified here). So the 2×350W bundle has to be wired in parallel.

findings.label: What's in the box
findings.value: 1 panel + 1 × 20 A MC4-to-XT60 solar charging cable (1.5 m). No parallel/Y connector listed.
findings.note: The page also lists the Elite 200 V2 as a compatible model, but says nothing about series or parallel wiring.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage / short-circuit current
findings.value: 24.6 V Voc, 10.8 A Isc per panel
findings.source_title: BLUETTI 200W Portable Solar Panel (BLUETTI US store)
findings.note: In series: 2 × 24.6 V = 49.2 V, within 12–60 V. In parallel: 2 × 10.8 A = 21.6 A of short-circuit current, over the 20 A input rating. So for this pair, series is the wiring that stays inside both limits. Price $399.00.

findings.label: In the box
findings.value: AC charging cable, documentation, the Elite 200 V2, grounding screw (no solar cable listed)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2+2*350W Solar (BLUETTI US store)
